title: Bullet Point Punctuation
keyIdea: Bullet points set out a list down the page, one item per line, after a lead-in that usually ends with a colon. The golden rule is consistency: every bullet in a list starts the same way, ends the same way and is the same kind of words. Bullets that are words or short phrases (a torch, warm socks) usually start with a small letter and have no full stop. Bullets that are full sentences (The bus leaves at nine.) start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. Each bullet should also run on from the lead-in in the same form, and the commas and the and of a sentence list are dropped.
familyTip: Write a packing list for a trip as bullets together, then swap papers and check each other's: does every bullet start the same way and end the same way? Read the lead-in before each bullet out loud to hear whether it fits.

visual.caption: Does each bullet need a full stop? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: We will be back by six

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sentence or phrase, spot the bullet that breaks the pattern, run on from the lead-in, make a list match, turn a sentence into bullets.

kid: Bullet points set out a list down the page. Each item gets its own line and its own dot. The line just before the list is the lead-in. It often ends with a colon, like You will need:

If a bullet is just a word or a short phrase, like a torch, start it with a small letter and put no full stop at the end. If a bullet is a whole sentence, like The bus leaves at nine, give it a capital letter and a full stop.
The big rule is to make every bullet match. If one bullet starts with a capital and the rest do not, it looks like a slip. The same goes for full stops.

Read the lead-in, then each bullet straight after it. To stay safe, you should wear a helmet works. To stay safe, you should using lights does not. When you turn a list in a sentence into bullets, drop the commas and the and.
adult: Ages 10 to 11. The national curriculum in England lists the punctuation of bullet points to list information in Year 6 (English Appendix 2), and the Years 5 to 6 writing programme asks pupils to use layout devices and punctuation accurately. Schools teach more than one house style, so the marking rule is that a list is consistent.

A common style, used by GOV.UK and many publishers, has a lead-in ending in a colon and bullets that read on from it. Bullets that are words or phrases start with a small letter and have no end punctuation. When bullets are full sentences, each starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. Every bullet should also have the same grammatical form, such as all starting with a verb.

Common mistakes: mixing capitals and small letters across bullets; a full stop on some bullets but not others; one full sentence among short phrases; a bullet that does not run on from the lead-in (you should using lights); and keeping the commas or the and from the sentence version of the list.

In the lab your child decides whether six bullets are sentences, finds the bullet that breaks the pattern in four lists, and drags the bullet that runs on from the lead-in into three lists. They switch capitals and full stops until two lists match a style, and turn three sentence lists into bullets.

practice.prompt: Which bullet fits this list? You will need: a hat, a scarf, …
practice.hint: Look at how the other bullets start and end.
practice.explain: The other bullets are short phrases with a small letter and no full stop, so gloves matches them.

practice.prompt: A sentence lists {n} items: a coat, a hat … and a drink. If you set them out as bullets, how many bullet lines do you need?
practice.hint: Each item gets its own line.
practice.explain: One item per line, so {n} items need {n} bullet lines. The commas and the and are dropped.

practice.prompt: A bullet says: The museum opens at ten. What should it end with?
practice.hint: Does it have a subject and a verb, and make sense alone?
practice.explain: It has a subject and a verb and makes sense alone, so it is a sentence and ends with a full stop.

practice.prompt: A list has {b} bullets. Every bullet is a whole sentence. How many full stops does the list need at the ends of the bullets?
practice.hint: Each sentence bullet ends with its own full stop.
practice.explain: Each of the {b} sentence bullets ends with a full stop, so {b} full stops.

practice.prompt: To make a kite, you need to: cut the paper, … Which bullet fits?
practice.hint: Read the lead-in, then the bullet straight after it.
practice.explain: you need to tie on the string runs on, and tie matches cut. The other two do not follow the lead-in.

pool.prompt: What is the main rule for punctuating bullet points?
choices: Every bullet in a list follows the same pattern.
Every bullet needs a capital and a full stop.
Bullets can be punctuated any way.
pool.hint: Think about what makes a list look right.
pool.explain: Consistency is the rule. Phrases do not need a capital or a full stop, but all the bullets must match.

pool.hint: Do all the bullets start and end the same way?
pool.explain: All three are short words with a small letter and no full stop. The others mix capitals or full stops.

pool.prompt: Our pet needs: food, water and a bed. As bullets, what goes on the last line?
pool.hint: What happens to the and and the commas?
pool.explain: Drop the and and the commas. Each item stands on its own line: a bed.

pool.prompt: Which bullet is a whole sentence?
pool.hint: Look for a subject and a verb.
pool.explain: Lunch is in the hall has a subject and a verb, so it is a sentence. The others are phrases.

pool.prompt: A list has {t} bullets. {s} of them start with a capital letter and the rest start small. Every bullet is a short phrase. How many bullets need fixing?
pool.hint: Phrases should start with a small letter.
pool.explain: The {s} bullets with capitals break the pattern, so {s} need fixing. The other {=t-s} are already right.

pool.prompt: At the farm we saw: three pigs, a black cow, … Which bullet fits?
pool.hint: Read At the farm we saw before each choice.
pool.explain: At the farm we saw two white goats runs on and matches the other noun phrases.

pool.prompt: Which mark usually ends the lead-in before a bullet list?
pool.hint: It looks like two dots, one above the other.
pool.explain: A colon points ahead to the list, as in You will need:

pool.prompt: In a list of short phrases, one bullet says: Some spoons are in it too. What is wrong?
choices: It is a whole sentence among phrases.
pool.hint: Is it the same kind of words as the others?
pool.explain: The other bullets are short phrases, so a full sentence breaks the pattern. Write some spoons instead.

pool.prompt: A sentence list of {n} items has commas between the items and an and before the last one. How many commas are dropped when it becomes bullets?
pool.hint: The last two items are joined by and, not a comma.
pool.explain: {n} items have {=n-1} gaps. One gap holds the and, so {=n-2} commas are dropped, along with the and.
